key_insight: A shot-efficient evolutionary search can optimize Clifford-deformed quantum error-correcting codes while accounting for both decoder choice and circuit-level noise, revealing better codes than brute-force search.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum engineers a practical way to tune error-correcting codes for specific hardware noise profiles without extra qubit overhead.
method: Treat the circuit, noise model, and decoder as a black box
Use Evolution-Based Best-arm Identification (EBBI) to search the exponentially large CD space efficiently
Benchmark on rotated surface code with PyMatching under strongly Z-biased noise
evidence_signal: In the abstract, EBBI is reported to find the optimal CD up to about 1100× fewer shots than random search at distance 3, and to converge to the believed-optimal CDs at distance 5 where random search does not.
watch_item: The best CD depends strongly on the exact noise model and decoder, so performance gains may not transfer without re-optimization on the target device.
paper_title: Decoder- and Noise-Aware Optimization Framework for Clifford-Deformed Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
